summary: Round-1 major (untested isEmptyRow branch) and minor (no keyboard-specific 4096-trim/PII test) are both genuinely closed by meaningful litmus tests. No new test-quality issues. Suite green.

round1_verification.item: Untested isEmptyRow defensive branch (row with empty/null buttons)
round1_verification.rationale: Input rows = [row("A"), row()] where the second row has an empty (non-null) buttons list — non-null, non-empty list, so the rows==null/isEmpty() conditions do NOT fire; only the rows.stream().anyMatch(isEmptyRow) branch catches it. Removing that anyMatch clause from the guard makes execution proceed to buildReplyKeyboardMarkup + send → CONTINUE instead of FAIL, so the test fails. Asserts FAIL + reasonCode 'empty_keyboard_rows' + sendText never(). Exercises exactly the buttons().isEmpty() sub-branch of isEmptyRow. The row() no-arg helper produces a KeyboardRow with an empty (not null) buttons list, which is the realistic malformed-snapshot shape.

Input keyboardText = 5000 chars. Asserts CONTINUE (over-length is not a failure), captured text hasSize(MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH) (fails if trimming/cap not applied via renderTrimmed → text stays 5000), WARN contains LOG_TEXT_TRIMMED (fails if no trim WARN emitted), and noneMatch('aaaa') confirms no rendered payload leaks into the log (PII guard). Mirrors the established message_trimsTextOver4096AndWarns idiom (line 159) adapted to the keyboard send path — verifies the renderTrimmed wiring on the new code path, not the renderer in isolation.
